head: bfe078b69dc691ecfd226d2872cff41dcb1b8360
classification_reasons: Blast radius: a new gate check (lesson_and_eval) is registered at CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'] and will park every future incident change at gate (e) on up to eight distinct conditions; this changes behavior for every project pinned to the new plugin version, not just this repository.

Size and shape: 18 real source/test files touched (new module plugin/lessons/index.py, new gate check in plugin/gate/checks.py + artifacts.py, two command-file rewrites, a template README rewrite, a new sdlc.yaml documented key) plus a version bump across both manifests — well beyond 'few files'.

The spec itself records several rounds of flagged concerns (tag vocabulary, Windows newline stability, the runbook field source) that were only closed this round; a spec with that history is not 'no open concern from the start', and the behavior (frontmatter parsing, generated index, a new deterministic gate check) is new code, not something the existing test suite covered before this change.
attempted: Intent: the artifact matches intent.md's proposed outcome point for point (frontmatter fields and sources, the generated index with its build/check CLI, the gate's lesson_and_eval check scoped to phase (e) only, the README rewrite, the sdlc.yaml documented key, the OPERATING_MODEL.md sentence); no scope drift found.

Spec and plan: walked plan.md's 'Files that change' list against the actual diff file-by-file (index.py, artifacts.py, checks.py, sdlc-deploy.md, sdlc-maintain.md, template/lessons/README.md, template/sdlc.yaml, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, both manifests, test_lessons.py, test_gate.py, test_commands_and_skills.py) — every file plan.md names is present and matches its description; the eight gate-check fail cases plan.md's Risk 2 and Proof sections enumerate are each present as a named test in tests/test_gate.py (missing lesson, two lesson files matching the glob, missing frontmatter field, prompt.md/checks.yaml missing, failing index.py check, dangling supersedes, supersedes target never retired, out-of-enum status), plus the phase-(e)-only guard test and the direct phase-(f) call proving the guard itself. All of spec.md's Flagged concerns are marked [x] decided with a concrete mechanism, not left open.

Proof: no test.log/build.log/lint.log are present yet (CI session; the runner replaces them after this review, per the brief's rule) so I did not treat their absence as a gap. Traced the parked preflight failure to its actual mechanism: tests/test_policy_skills.py's `project` fixture runs the real /sdlc-init (sdlc_init.py) over a fresh git checkout, which copies template/lessons/README.md as untracked (hence 'added') content; the pre-fix README's heading text 'its eval (build guide steps 36, 37...)' matched the security-baseline scanner's `eval\s*\(` dangerous-call pattern, failing the fixture-is-clean assertion the owner quoted. Confirmed by grep that no 'eval(' or 'eval (' pattern remains anywhere under template/, plugin/commands/sdlc-deploy.md or plugin/commands/sdlc-maintain.md after the fix commit, and that the two legitimate uses of the substring ('lesson_and_eval(ctx)') are exempted by the scanner's own `(?<![\w.])` lookbehind, so the fix is both necessary and sufficient and introduces no new risk. verifier.md's direct CLI/function exercises (index.py build/check with class-normalisation, staleness, CRLF tolerance; lesson_and_eval called directly for the pass case, the phase-(f) short-circuit, a missing-lesson fail and a dangling-supersedes fail) line up with the diff's actual code.

Blast radius: grepped the diff for guardrail paths (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, this repo's root sdlc.yaml) — none touched. Checked sdlc.yaml: risk_list — spec.md and the plan correctly argue none of auth/money/production-config/data-migration applies, and I found nothing in the diff that moves stored data or changes a schema; the only new data shape is markdown frontmatter plus a generated, never-hand-edited index file. The new gate check is scoped by `ctx.status.entry_route == "incident" and ctx.phase == "e"`, verified in checks.py and covered by a direct-call test and a kept, unmodified regression test name for gate (f), so the stated main risk (the check firing at the wrong phase or silently doing nothing) has test coverage pointed exactly at it.

Policies: data-conventions (no personal/sensitive field; every new frontmatter field is a constant, date, tag or internal identifier), security-baseline (the eval() false-positive was the one real hit, now fixed and verified absent), definition-of-done's split between deterministic gate checks and advisory eval-content review is respected (lesson_and_eval checks only shape, not eval quality) — all applied, none silently skipped.

Tests: read the new tests/test_lessons.py and the new tests/test_gate.py cases in full; they exercise the actual ordering, retired/unsorted grouping, stale-marker and CRLF-tolerance behavior through the real build()/check() functions (not mocks), and the gate-check tests call lesson_and_eval directly with fixtures that isolate exactly one broken precondition per test, so a broken check (e.g. a wrong glob, a swapped boolean, a missing supersedes-status check) would fail these tests, not pass silently. No pre-existing test was weakened; this is a feature change and the existing gate-(f) test is confirmed unchanged by its absence from the diff.
